procedure.description: neuroplasty and/or transposition, median nerve at carpal tunnel

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 64721 (neuroplasty and/or transposition, median nerve at carpal tunnel) with date of service 2026-05-29. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish failure of conservative treatment or electrodiagnostic confirmation.

criteria.text: Symptoms consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome, such as nocturnal paresthesias in the median nerve distribution with a positive Tinel or Phalen sign, present for at least 6 weeks.
Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management including neutral wrist splinting, together with NSAIDs, activity modification, or a corticosteroid injection.
Electrodiagnostic testing (nerve conduction study or electromyography) confirming median neuropathy at the wrist, unless thenar atrophy or constant sensory loss is present.

chart.text: Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Blood pressure check. 130 over 78 today, 132 over 78 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

42 year old woman here for the right hand, referred by the PCP. Works on a keyboard all day. Discussed carpal tunnel release, open versus endoscopic, recovery. Her history otherwise: seasonal allergies. Surgeries: no prior surgery. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, lives alone. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. 3 months of numbness and tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers on the right, wakes her at night, shakes it out. Positive Tinel at the right wrist, Phalen positive in about 20 seconds. Some early thenar weakness, no atrophy yet. Splinted at night for 10 weeks, naproxen twice a day, moved the mouse to the other hand, and had a steroid shot in the right carpal tunnel from the PCP that helped for about three weeks and wore off.
Back to review the plan for the right hand. Still symptomatic. Wants to proceed. Vitals today 142 over 84, pulse 74.
A1c came back 5.7. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.6, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 231, LDL 151, HDL 38, triglycerides 113. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Pre-op. Consent signed for right open carpal tunnel release under local with sedation. Marked.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-3 (ncs); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
